newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended Friday a shade up from New York's previous close on overseas buying in the afternoon, but activity was thin as the market remained rattled by Thursday's sharp jump, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$351.00/50 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$350.40/90 close on Thursday.
"The market moved a bit higher because of Swiss buying," said one dealer at a local bullion firm.
Other dealers reported light speculative buying from Europe in afternoon trade.
But activity was thin and players unwilling to make a move in an unpredictable market, dealers said.
"Too many people lost money," said another gold source.
New York spot gold on Thursday ended quoted $350.40/90 an ounce compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $345.00.
Physical buying in Asia slowed after the price jump, dealers said.
Local tael gold ended HK$52 higher at HK$3,243 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at nil.
